about: Questions waiting on Scott and the record of how each was answered, for the Family History Site Guide. Rendered with docs/planning/site-guide.md; binding rulings are in its Decisions table. Proposal material only; nothing here is published site copy or a capability claim.

questions.title: Make this Site Guide the main document builders follow?
questions.why: The Project Philosophy is about 1,900 lines of trust rules, language rules and evidence history with no page inventory. Builders need one concrete source.

options.label: Yes, canonical
options.detail: The guide leads; the philosophy becomes the trust-rules and history reference.

options.label: Keep as draft
options.detail: The philosophy stays official until the whole guide is reviewed.

questions.reason: Builders need one concrete source, and Scriptures made the same move on 27 September.

questions.title: Organize research around Questions, or add a separate Projects block?
questions.why: A Question holds the AI's plan, what was searched, found and not found, and the conclusion. A Project is a folder for a piece of research work.

options.label: Questions
options.detail: One research container that nests.

options.label: Projects
options.detail: A familiar folder with no built-in sense of what is being answered.

options.label: Both
options.detail: Projects hold Questions; two blocks, two pages, more AI tools.

questions.reason: Nesting Questions covers what a Project folder would do without a second container.

answered.note: Projects hold Questions; Questions still nest. Projects also suit helping someone else or a client's request.

questions.title: Call a source-backed statement a Fact, Claim or Detail?
questions.why: The word appears on every Person page and in every AI tool. Each statement has a state: Proposed, Accepted, Disputed or Rejected.

options.label: Facts
options.detail: Friendly; the states show a fact can be wrong.

options.label: Claims
options.detail: Precise in genealogy terms, a little colder.

options.label: Details
options.detail: Soft but vague.

questions.reason: The everyday word, with the states carrying the caution.

questions.title: One family workspace per account, or several trees?
questions.why: One workspace keeps every person once; several trees suit separate research for different families.

options.label: One workspace
options.detail: Branches are views from a home person.

options.label: Several trees
options.detail: Separate containers; risk of duplicates and split sources.

questions.reason: Avoids duplicates and hard merges later.

answered.note: Each tree is a separate workspace switched like a profile. Resources (websites, software), Preferences, Instructions, the AI connection and the Queue bridge trees. Reasons: helping other people with their trees; genealogists serving clients. Risks to be navigated with care.

questions.title: Keep photos inside Sources, or a separate Photos collection?
questions.why: Every file needs one home. A photo is often evidence too.

options.label: Inside Sources
options.detail: One home per file; the Sources grid is the gallery.

options.label: Separate Photos
options.detail: Simpler model; evidence photos need a Source as well.

questions.reason: Keeps the evidence and the picture together.

answered.note: Each file is connectable to every person, place, event, Project and Story it matters to, with face tags, portrait crops and AI-suggested connections the person accepts.

questions.title: Store family memories as Notes and family-memory Sources, or as their own block?
questions.why: What the person remembers differs from an account recorded from a relative, which can be evidence.

options.label: Notes and Sources
options.detail: The person's words stay theirs; a relative's account can back a claim labelled as lore. Rename the Memories tab.

options.label: Memories block
options.detail: Easy to find, but cannot back a claim without also becoming a Source.

questions.reason: Lore becomes usable, clearly labelled evidence.

questions.title: Add Topics as a main block for reusable historical context?
questions.why: Context such as a war, migration, faith or trade touches many lives and should be researched once.

options.label: Add Topics
options.detail: Context saved once and shown everywhere it applies.

options.label: Places only
options.detail: Context that is not about one place has nowhere good to live.

questions.reason: Context research adds up over time instead of being redone per ancestor.

questions.title: Let signing in approve your AI, or keep a second approval step in Settings?
questions.why: Today a new connection sees no tools until the person ticks seven permissions. The family rule (1 September) is that Allow is the approval. The 6 October sibling comparison recommended keeping the extra step because records include living people.

options.label: Sign-in approves
options.detail: Hard limits stay; living-person and private records unreadable to the AI until reviewed.

options.label: Keep second step
options.detail: One extra approval screen after Allow.

questions.reason: Protects living people record by record and matches every other Assist site.

questions.title: Leave sharing trees with relatives and clients out of the first builds?
questions.why: Unlisted links and collaborators (AWF-0014/0015) multiply every privacy rule.

options.label: Not yet
options.detail: Core blocks and trees first; sharing one tree later.

options.label: Include sharing now
options.detail: Slower, with privacy rules on every new page.

questions.reason: Separate trees set up clean sharing later.

answered.note: Existing guarded public-story publishing stays. Future sharing is per tree.

questions.title: Do Topics belong to the account or to each tree?
questions.why: Trees are separate workspaces. A Topic such as a war or a migration is useful context in any tree, but its connections to people belong to that tree.

options.label: Account level
options.detail: One Topic reused in every tree; its connections stay inside each tree.

options.label: Per tree
options.detail: Each tree keeps its own Topics; context is researched again per tree.

questions.reason: Context research is worth doing once, and keeping connections per tree preserves separation.

changes: The Site Guide is canonical (edition 2), with the Project Philosophy kept as the trust-boundary and evidence reference.
Projects join the building blocks and hold Questions.
Several trees, each a separate workspace, with account-level Resources, Preferences, Instructions, AI connection and Queue.
Photos stay inside Sources and connect to everything they matter to.
Signing in approves the AI; no new sharing in the first builds.
